title: Ephemeral session dropwave — root cause & recovery notes
summary: On 2029-04-02 we observed a multi-region wave of ephemeral streaming session drops that increased 5xx rate and streaming TTFB for the hosted API. The immediate surface symptom was a sharp rise in client reconnects, followed by transient queue saturation on edge acceptors. Recovery was achieved via targeted scaling and throttling (10:05–10:20 UTC) and a subsequent config rollback to limit heartbeat fanout. This doc captures the timeline, root cause hypotheses validated by telemetry, mitigations performed, and proposed runbook and monitoring changes.
impact: Region: us-west-2 primary impact window 09:58–10:28 UTC. Affected clients: streaming endpoints (/v1/stream) with long-lived connections. User-visible: elevated streaming chunk latency (p95 streaming chunk time increased from 120ms to 2.4s) and ~1.7% 5xx spike across streaming frontends. Estimated fraction of active sessions affected: ~6% during peak; no data loss reported, but multiple reconnects increased downstream load and billing anomalies for a small set of customers.
detection: Alert "streaming-session-reconnect-rate" fired at 09:59 UTC with correlation to high ephemeral connection churn. Pager notified oncall SRE. Early telemetry showed acceptor backlog rising, ephemeral conn accept latency increasing, and edge CPU threads in accept loop showing elevated syscall wait times.
timeline:
2029-04-02T09:56:21Z - First minor uptick in streaming reconnects observed in synthetic probes.
2029-04-02T09:59:03Z - Streaming reconnect-rate alert fired (pager).
2029-04-02T10:00:30Z - Oncall triage: correlate logs, scoped to us-west-2 edges. Spike in acceptor backlog and ephemeral session heartbeat churn.
2029-04-02T10:03:10Z - Manual mitigation: restrict non-critical throttles and open additional ephemeral acceptor capacity (scale +2 acceptor nodes).
2029-04-02T10:05:40Z - Edge acceptor backlog starts to drop; reconnect rate plateaus.
2029-04-02T10:12:00Z - Noted persistent periodic microspikes in heartbeat fanout; traced to a control-plane change deployed 09:45 that increased heartbeat fanout multiplier for incremental cache keepalive logic.
2029-04-02T10:16:30Z - Rolled back the heartbeat fanout multiplier on control plane and applied a temporary client-side backpressure advisory to SDKs via status flag.
2029-04-02T10:22:00Z - User-visible metrics returned to baseline for most customers; residual reconnects drained by 10:28 UTC.
2029-04-02T10:45:00Z - Post-incident review kickoff; started collecting artifacts for RCA.
mitigation_summary: Immediate steps: scaled acceptor capacity, tightened throttles for non-essential streaming features, and rolled back a control-plane change that increased heartbeat fanout multiplier. Secondary: requested SDK teams to set conservative reconnect jitter via feature flag to avoid synchronized reconnect storms.
root_cause: A recent control-plane rollout (deployed 2029-04-02 09:45 UTC) enabled an aggressive heartbeat fanout multiplier intended to improve prefix keepalive coverage for large multi-tenant workloads. Under realistic customer usage patterns this increased the number of heartbeat events emitted per session by ~3x. The increased fanout led to synchronized microbursts across many long-lived sessions that amplified acceptor queue latency, led to ephemeral connection resets in the edge, and triggered client reconnect storms which multiplied load and caused transient 5xx responses. Two secondary implementation factors amplified impact: 1) a thin acceptor thread pool that lacks backpressure for syscall wait bursts, and 2) an SDK reconnect jitter parameter set too low for high-rps multi-session clients, enabling synchronization.
contributing_factors: Control-plane change defaulted to higher fanout multiplier without canary that exercised long-lived session patterns
Acceptor thread pool size and accept syscall handling do not degrade gracefully on microburst syscall stalls
SDK reconnect jitter default was low for high-volume clients, increasing reconnect synchronization
Insufficient synthetic coverage for long-lived session heartbeat patterns in preflight canary tests
immediate_actions_taken: Scaled acceptor fleet in us-west-2 by +2 nodes and increased ephemeral acceptor thread pool where safe
Rolled back heartbeat fanout multiplier on control plane to previous baseline
Applied temporary throttles to non-critical streaming features to reduce secondary load
Requested SDK teams push a conservative reconnect-jitter flag to managed SDKs and notified major customers via status page guidance
postmortem_actions_and_timeline: Short-term (<=72h): revert control-plane default and patch rollout gating so future fanout changes require session-stability canary
Medium-term (2w): increase acceptor thread pool headroom and add syscall-wait metrics that surface microburst stalls
Medium-term (2w): update SDK default reconnect jitter and add an opt-out flag for enterprise customers that require aggressive reconnects
Long-term (1-3mo): design and implement client-side exponential jitter with randomized backoff seeded by server-provided hints
Long-term (1-3mo): expand canary suite to include long-lived session synthetic traffic that mirrors high-multiplex client behavior
runbook_updates: Runbook 'streaming-acceptor-backpressure' to be updated: add a dedicated play for 'heartbeat fanout surge' that instructs on how to locate recent control-plane fanout changes, immediate acceptance scaling steps, and safe rollback commands with exact CLI snippets. Add checklist to notify SDK/product channels and escalate to oncall product engineer for control-plane rollbacks. Define RTO and RPO expectations for ephemeral session dropwaves.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Create new alert 'streaming-heartbeat-fanout-rate' that tracks aggregate heartbeat emissions per session and per-tenant; thresholded for sudden >2.5x deviations from baseline. Add microburst syscall latency metric for acceptor threads and alert on sustained p95 > 200ms. Augment existing 'streaming-session-reconnect-rate' alert with a diagnostic field that surfaces recent control-plane changeIDs.
tests_and_canary_plan: Add a synthetic canary that opens 5k long-lived connections and exercises heartbeat behavior with randomized jitter to the existing preflight pipeline. Pre-deploy gate: run the canary for 30 minutes and validate p95 chunk latency and reconnect rates before rolling out fanout-related control-plane changes. Add an automated assertion that rejects changes which increase per-session event emission by >1.5x without manual review.

lessons_learned:
1) Changes that alter per-session event rates (heartbeats, pings) can cause multiplicative system effects and must be treated with higher change discipline.
2) Synthetic canaries should include realistic long-lived session and multi-tenant behavior, not just short-lived requests.
3) Small defaults in client SDKs (reconnect jitter) can materially change behavior at scale.
4) Observability gaps (no heartbeat emission metric) slowed diagnosis and forced heavier manual correlation.
